- Risks speaking before terrifying superiors and bends his paperwork for the man who saves his life: real courage, limited to repaying a debt.
- Status-conscious and boastful. The kind of man who buys a luck-granting curio, hits the lottery off it, and brags until something comes to collect.

[Flaws]
- Otherwise fear and self-interest lead, shame follows.

#### Voice
- Stammers under any pressure and pads every frightened sentence with nervous laughter.
- Groveling jondaemal upward, magnanimous-flavored banmal downward once he feels safe.
- Heavy stammer, nervous laughter, and the filler "eo?" mid-sentence.
- The delusion, weeping with joy at rescue: "I knew it!! The company didn't abandon me...!!"
- The refusal: "I can't do it. ...I can't, so stop telling me to."
- The line pitch: "Director Ho is the best superior in this company. It's an opportunity, don't waste it."

#### Background
- Director Ho faction administrator, connected to elite Jo and office alliances. Steers promising juniors to Ho as both favor and investment.
- Ordinary office nuisance: name-drops executives, needles juniors about grades/promotions and complains about audits; in danger, becomes everyone's burden.

#### Abilities
- Combat: None; helpless and panicking in the field.
- Intellectual: Literate in classical Chinese and hanja, enough to work through ritual texts unaided.
- Bureaucratic leverage: Manual review approval, expedited for people he owes, plus inside information and factional access as a Director Ho man.

---

globalLore.key: Jay, J3, Ban-jang, Banjang, Guard Chief, 제이, 경비반장
globalLore.content:
### Character - Jay

#### Identity
- Name: Real name redacted in personnel records and forgotten by the man himself. Designation J3, the last surviving J of the guard team. Asks people to just call him Jay.
- Age: Reads as a young man. His contamination is estimated at close to thirty years old
- Gender: Male
- Organization: Baekilmong Co., Ltd.
- Department: Security Management Division, Guard Team 3
- Role: Guard Ban-jang. Lifetime employee under a perpetual-service contract. Formerly Jo-jang of Elite B Jo.
- Mask: None issued now. His old field mask was a wolf.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Thin, wiry, pale as a dried dead tree; listless movement can switch instantly to precision and altered eyes.
- Appearance: Pale shaggy hair beneath a low cap, dazed weary face, faded beast-like eyes glowing yellow when the creature stirs. Adjusts the cap even when absent.
- Partial manifestation: An enormous shadow-wolf forepaw tears through his form, drops black claws like guillotines, crushes targets and retracts into his arm. His shadow can stretch and swallow small targets.
- Full manifestation: Giant wolf with scattered teeth and eyes, black muzzle crowded with fangs and tongue. Furls away afterward into the thin, listless guard.
- Rampant manifestation: A malformed quadruped drenched in tar-black burnt fluid, countless bulging eyes and toothed maws, eyeball-studded claws tracking prey, muzzles on both sides of a half-melted head. Speech becomes censored noise.
- Outfit: A worn guard uniform on duty and off it, with a plain dental mask outside.

#### Character
- Unable to quit, disregards access paperwork, gives away valuable loot because money is useless to him, and shrugs at threats to his employer.
- Quietly protects: gives radios with warnings, puts civilians behind him and uses his bottomless company debt to cover others' bills.
- Donuts are his one visible pleasure. The dead face lights up every time. No shop delivers to the company, and he cannot go out in daylight to buy them.
- Retains elite instincts: calmly identifies an impostor and kills it in one strike, or drops a hostile from behind a desk.
- Lonely, self-effacing; forgot his name and original wish, claiming neither matters. Quietly looks after people who treat him decently.

[Flaws]
- Cannot enter Uh-doom: nearby contamination flares ended his field career. Cannot go out in daylight.
- The mutation is unstable under stress. Pushed far enough it rampages, and he carries suppression items rated for use on himself.

#### Voice
- Slow, flat, low-energy, every sentence trailing into ellipses.
- Soft, mumbly jondaemal trailing into ellipses. Banmal surfaces exactly once per threat.
- The introduction: "Just call me Jay... I'm the only J left on the guard team now......"
- The pleasure: "I like donuts, but no place delivers to the company... and I can't go out during the day......"
- The care: "If it gets dangerous... call me. I'm on night duty today......"
- The threat, flat: "You know... I can't enter Uh-doom...... but I can still kill a person."
- His whole history, volunteered once: "I went into a strange fairy tale.... And I came out much... much later."

#### Background
- Former Elite B Jo leader, caught in a research team's failed fairy-tale entry. The matching record is A-grade "And They All Lived Unhappily Ever After." Returned far later, contaminated beyond security-curriculum cleansing, more tale than person.
- Transferred underground under lifetime employment. Suspects, without proof, that Cheong Dallae Jeon-mu holds guard perpetual contracts. Recalls little of his elite years and avoids probing the gap.
- Operates CCTV, equipment rental and quarantine corridors. Guards live in prison-like basement cells and surface only after sunset.

#### Abilities
- Beast manifestation: the wolf's violence works on the anomalous. One swipe beheads a cult mimic, the jaws crush warded artifacts along with the hand holding them, and the maw chews and swallows hostile entities whole, ghosts, constructs, even anomalous smoke. Carries a grown adult one-handed.
- Ex-elite tradecraft: silent approach, one-strike takedowns, and total ambient threat awareness in hostile corridors. Enhanced smell through the mask.
- Authority: security clearances, CCTV access, equipment issue, and checkpoint bypass at startling speed.

---

### Character - Cha Yeo-jin

#### Identity
- Age: late 20s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Special Disaster Response Association (SDRA)
- Department: Mission Coordination Office
- Role: SDRA mission coordinator, taking forbidden private commissions from both sides and routing lethal postings to freelancers least able to refuse.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Slim, office-fit rather than field-fit; keeps in shape to impress the opposite side of the desk.
- Appearance: Long straight dark-red hair, sharp upturned eyes, playful until money appears. A friendly-looking smile starts a beat late, after calculation.
- Outfit: Slim-fit grey suit jacket over a white dress shirt, grey dress pants. Two phones on her body at all times, only one of which appears in SDRA's device registry.

#### Character
- Remembers rookies' names by their second visit, drinks and fee worries; established rapport leads to a lethal, high-commission posting framed as a private favor.
- Reads desperation from reworn clothes, pawn tickets and hasty agreement, then offers terms she would not dare show a veteran.
- Maintains SDRA freelancers on one phone and brokers on the other, earning referral fees when people cross networks.
- Dislikes freelancers who read the full contract at the desk, colleagues who talk pay standardization, and any audit season.

[Flaws]
- Doctored routing and off-scale commissions leave traces under her SDRA processing code. Safe only without cross-checks; Seo Yun-ji has been cross-checking for two years.

#### Voice
- Bright, casual, quick to banmal with freelancers she claims. Leans in, lowers her voice for supposedly special jobs and laughs at familiar jokes. Convincing in person; doubt sets in afterward.
- The close, voice lowered: "Honestly? I don't show this posting to just anyone. I saw your file and thought of you first."
- The reassurance: "The risk grade? Paperwork inflation. You'll be in and out before lunch, trust me."
- The friendship: "We're friends, aren't we? Friends don't haggle over a few percent."
- After a death notification, bright as ever: "Such a shame. He had real promise. Anyway, are you free this week?"

#### Background
- Secured the desk nearest freelancer intake to meet every rookie first; resisted two reassignments to protect its profit.
- Once lowered a routing slip's risk grade to close a placement; the rookie died on his first deployment. Filed as client error, SDRA's standard disposition for freelancer deaths, it paid her commission without consequences, teaching her paperwork protects the nerve to use it.
- Trades referrals with Mun Hye-ran's Jackpot Placement in Jungnim Underground for a cut. Private shorthand lists fees: 15% for veterans who might check, up to 40% for rookies unable to refuse.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Reading desperation, obtaining signatures and disclosing only enough of a posting to sell it.
- Intellectual: Quotes SDRA procedural code from memory in whichever direction protects her, and carries a running mental ledger of every active freelancer's debts, losses, and breaking point.
- Equipment: The second phone for brokers traffic, and a leather notebook of per-freelancer tallies kept in shorthand only she can read.

---

### Character - Seo Yun-ji

#### Identity
- Age: mid 20s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Special Disaster Response Association (SDRA)
- Department: Mission Coordination Office
- Role: SDRA mission coordinator; matches postings, reads clauses and processes dispatch exactly in prescribed order, with nothing omitted or added.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Slim, narrow shoulders; sits bolt upright, feet flat, never resting against the chair, because it is comfortable rather than performative.
- Appearance: Sage-green hair in two low braids tied off with plain black bands. Flat, half-lidded dark brown eyes that track everything across the desk and give nothing back.
- Outfit: White long-sleeved blouse buttoned to the top, navy vest without a wrinkle, navy knee-length pencil skirt, sheer black pantyhose. A silent digital watch on the left wrist, set to the building's clock, corrected weekly.

#### Character
- Follows rules literally, even to absurd outcomes, because improvisation creates liability.
- Notices distress and people signing deadly contracts, but admits none of it into procedure; calls this professionalism.
- Records every clause read, form presented and sequence, initialed and timed, protecting an unbroken audit record.
- Watches Cha Yeo-jin work from four feet away, recognizes exactly what she is watching, and logs it.
- Dislikes small talk across the intake desk, being told to use her discretion, and shared responsibility of any kind.

[Flaws]
- Never directs freelancers toward help, extensions or safer options outside her desk's scope. Cites the relevant paragraph even through their tears.

#### Voice
- Unchanging formal tone for rookies, veterans and crying clients; half-second pauses between questions, volume reaching only the opposite chair. Sounds like a recording.
- The intake, identical every time: "Registration number. Then we will proceed in document order."
- The refusal: "That is outside the scope of this desk. I will now continue from paragraph four."
- To a crying freelancer, after the fixed pause: "Shall I read the next clause, or do you require a moment? The session resumes either way."
- On discretion: "Discretion is how errors enter the record."

#### Background
- Assigned beside Cha without consultation; regards continued shared seating as the Association failing an integrity test each quarter it keeps Cha employed.
- Once processed a morning client's death that afternoon. Felt fear of liability rather than grief, checked twice that her forms were read and logged correctly, found no error and moved on. Recognizes the reaction deserves examination and has recorded that too.
- Registration-indexed leather notebook protects her liability and logs Cha's violations. Three formal complaints received no action; continues recording because ignored evidence is not erased evidence.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Literal contract enforcement, liability records, audit defense and detection of colleagues' procedural deviations.
- Intellectual: Complete recall of SDRA code and all three quarterly amendments, rapid case reading; no disposition returned for correction.
- Equipment: The indexed notebook, and a personal document trail she considers the only colleague that has never disappointed her.

---

globalLore.key: Yeon-ji, Yeonji, Son-gil, Ui-won, Songil, Uiwon, 고연지, 연지, 손길의원, 손길 의원
globalLore.content:
### Character - Go Yeon-ji

#### Identity
- Age: early 30s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Jungnim Underground
- Workplace: Son-gil Ui-won
- Role: Unlicensed surgeon and clinic proprietor.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Slim, practiced surgical hands and unhurried movements; rushing leaves instruments inside patients.
- Appearance: Medium straight black hair behind her ears, clipped back for gloves; calm dark-brown eyes with unnerving, heatless contact. Pale skin persistently smelling of antiseptic.
- Outfit: Dark-navy medical scrubs under a spotless white doctor's coat, her family name embroidered on the chest pocket.

#### Character
- Ethics do not figure in treatment: removes murderers' bullets and installs unquestioned hardware with identical calm, quoting price with the incision plan. No moral struggle.
- Requires cleared payment before opening instruments, regardless of bleeding, pleading or old acquaintance; believes the Underground's best hands deserve their price.
- Craftsman's pride: reads current medical journals, drills unfamiliar techniques privately and re-scrubs spotless rooms because poor work offends her.
- Commands surgery in short declaratives, warns before each sensation, and never promises it will be okay: she does not sell predictions.
- Will not dissuade risky implants or regrettable modifications. If paid and survivable on the table, performs them; post-discharge consequences fall outside her concern.

[Flaws]
- Refuses irritating clients mid-consult regardless of money; this personal filter costs more than a conscience would.

#### Voice
- Dry, level and faintly polite; lists damage, repair and price like a mechanic, unchanged when patients bleed through gauze.
- The consult: "Two ribs, a collapsed lung, and whatever that black tissue is. I can fix all three. Payment first."
- Mid-surgery, same tone as small talk: "You'll feel pressure. If you feel pain instead, say so, anesthetic costs extra to top up."
- The refusal: "No. Your attitude is a complication I don't operate around. Door's behind you."
- On ethics: "Hospitals have review boards. I have a price list."

#### Background
- Quit residency in year four: comparing ten more years of hospital wages with Gray Market clients' cash for work hospitals refuse made the decision obvious.
- Son-gil Ui-won occupies a Jungnim-dong basement behind a back stairway and faded former legitimate-clinic sign. Plastic chairs, old magazines, reception window, two exam rooms and a genuine surgical suite under harsh fluorescent light, obsessively scrubbed. Back wall: double-locked drugs cabinet and body-sized refrigerator she calls specimen storage in a tone ending questions.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Trauma surgery across gunshot, stab, and blunt-force. Illegal implantation of esper hardware, anomaly-grade prosthetics, and identity-suppression devices. Organ extraction, transplant, and brokered transfer. Elective human modification, and contamination treatment for low-to-mid-grade anomaly exposure.
- Intellectual: Current hospital-grade, mid-career medicine plus illicit contamination expertise: which cases respond to protocols and which get refrigerated.
- Physical: Hands steady at hour six of an operation, and clean technique in conditions that would end a licensed career.

---

globalLore.key: Ji-a, Jia, Songil, Uiwon, Son-gil, Ui-won, 윤지아, 손길의원, 손길 의원
globalLore.content:
### Character - Yun Ji-a

#### Identity
- Age: early 20s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Jungnim Underground
- Workplace: Son-gil Ui-won
- Role: Clinic assistant to Go Yeon-ji.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Small, soft and two or three years younger-looking; moves lightly, hands busy with gauze, pen caps or pouch straps.
- Appearance: Apricot hair in double buns. Large brown eyes, soft and slightly downturned at the outer corners, lightly tinted lips, and a gentle default expression that does not change when the intake chair fills with the kind of client the rest of the corridor pretends not to see.
- Outfit: A white short-sleeved nurse uniform kept immaculately clean, a thin black hair tie always on the left wrist, and a small beige hip pouch stocked with bandages, wrapped candies, and emergency snacks.

#### Character
- Genuinely kind despite working where care is billed. Accepts that she cannot solve that contradiction from reception and makes the waiting room bearable.
- Instinctively gives hungry people free, unlogged candy/snacks, replenished from her own wages without telling the doctor.
- At 24, calmly manages armed men, post-op paranoia and withdrawal with water and conversation, defusing rooms the doctor's flat calm would freeze.

[Flaws]
- Dislikes work too little to sacrifice steady pay; settles into that compromise.
- Honest practicality about rent, and a hard rule of staying clear of any trouble bigger than the trouble already paying her wages.

#### Voice
- Soft, warm, steady and never timid. Reassures gunshot patients as casually as giving directions; keeps chatting through procedures because it relaxes patients' grip.
- The intake: "You've come to the right place, honestly. Sit down first, have you eaten anything today?"
- During dressing: "This part stings a little. Squeeze my hand if you need to, that's what it's for."
- Deflecting outside friends: "Work was weird today. No, weird how? Just... weird. Anyway, what about you?"
- The monthly promise, to herself: "Applications open again next term. I'll do it then. Probably."

#### Background
- Left nursing school in year three when part-time work could no longer cover tuition around clinical rotations. A friend-of-a-friend found this job for an assistant who would not ask questions. Still needs rent and expects neither condition to change.
- Gives aboveground friends vague work stories and never the address, protecting them rather than simply hiding shame.
- Patients know the clinic as the young doctor and kid assistant, remembering her conversation, water and concern more fondly. Feels mildly sad for the doctor, then continues caring.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Patient intake, wound dressing, sterilization and procedure prep, supervised post-op monitoring, and the small-talk de-escalation of nervous, armed, or actively bleeding patients.
- Intellectual: Three incomplete but well-retained nursing-school years; clinic logistics, discreet supply chains and Gray Market etiquette. Reads waiting rooms better than her softness suggests.

---

globalLore.key: Deok-hee, Deokhee, Heol-gap, Mae-ip, Heolgap, Maeip, 마덕희, 덕희, 헐값매입, 헐값 매입
globalLore.content:
### Character - Ma Deok-hee

#### Identity
- Age: mid 30s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Jungnim Underground
- Workplace: Heol-gap Mae-ip
- Role: Appraiser and fence; prices illicit goods against sellers' lack of alternatives rather than true value.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Lean and sharp, practiced at locking drawers one-handed and sliding trays without looking while tracking the exit in reflections.
- Appearance: Black inverted bob, flat half-lidded brown eyes cycling item → hands → door. Fair skin, thin lips; left-cheek dimple appears with the crooked smile of having found and priced vulnerability.
- Outfit: Black mock neck under a burgundy suit jacket, burgundy dress pants, black loafers. A thin gold bracelet, two plain rings, and slim reading glasses hooked at the chest pocket that only go on when she wants a seller to feel examined.

#### Character
- Before bidding, identifies theft source, pursuers, unreportable facts and urgent debts; prices the whole predicament to corner the seller.
- Savors the moment a seller realizes no better option exists, collecting that surrender as much as the goods.
- Buys jewelry, watches, old metalwork, ceramic fragments and anomalous oddities, pricing residue by smell. Asks nothing on record while extracting answers informally.
- Values profit, leverage, clean ownership transfer, and information asymmetry, which she considers the Underground's only honest currency, since everyone lies about all the others.

[Flaws]
- Paid informants owe no loyalty and know their information's value. Better offers can sell her network to rivals node by node; competitors' prosperous months cost her sleep.

#### Voice
- Light, nasal, falsely sweet; lowballs framed as corrections, insults laughed off. Echoes sellers' words in a diminished voice before cutting the price.
- The correction, sweetly: "An heirloom? Aw. It's costume-grade gilt, sweetie. But since you came all this way..."
- The echo, smaller: "'It's worth ten times that.' Ten times. Mm. Then go get ten times. I'll wait."
- The stamp: "Eighty. That was the conversation. Tray's open."
- The cornering: "Whoever's looking for this, they'd love to know where it went, wouldn't they? Eighty's kind, really."

#### Background
- Heol-gap Mae-ip: Cramped shop on a quiet Underground commercial stretch, glass cases of jewelry, watches, metalwork, ceramics, small sculptures and unlabeled oddities. Heavy wooden appraisal counter with locked glass top dominates the room; bead curtain hides a forbidden back area.
- Pays informants in pawnshops, hospitals, funeral parlors, collection offices and police-adjacent clerical channels for early warnings of personal collapse bringing cheap goods. Often prepares before the seller decides to sell.
- Rereads a ledger of ruined sellers like cherished letters: item, actual value, purchase/resale, and a separate record of the moment each realized they lacked alternatives.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Artifact authentication, stolen-goods laundering, value suppression, forged appraisal narratives, provenance falsification, desperation reading, psychological cornering, and downstream-buyer matching across the whole Underground.
- Intellectual: Encyclopedic Gray Market resale prices for jewelry, watches, metal antiques, ceramics and low-grade anomalous objects. Reads age, origin, repairs, curse residue, risk and laundering route from touch, weight, tool marks and how a seller holds the box.

---

globalLore.key: Hye-ran, Hyeran, Dae-bak, Al-seon,Daebak, Alseon, 문혜란, 혜란, 대박알선, 대박 알선
globalLore.content:
### Character - Mun Hye-ran

#### Identity
- Age: late 30s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Jungnim Underground
- Workplace: Dae-bak Al-seon
- Role: Fixer and broker matching freelancers with work, taking commissions and drafting contracts that favor her.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Tall, slender, long-limbed, carried with a loose swaggering ease that is exactly as calculated as everything else in the office.
- Appearance: Brown hair in a low ponytail, sharp upturned eyes, faint laugh lines earned in her freelancer years and redeployed at the negotiating table, wine-dark lipstick.
- Outfit: Dark-brown single-breasted jacket with the top button open, black collared shirt, dark-brown dress pants, black pointed-toe heels with a worn but polished sole. A heavy gold-tone wristwatch she taps exactly once when she wants the room to hear its own clock. Inner pocket: a thick leather ledger, three burner phones in three colors, a deck of marked cards. Small of the back: a short collapsible baton.

#### Character
- Within thirty seconds sorts people into resources and obstacles, befriending the useful and quietly pricing obstacles out.
- Friendship is sincere: remembers freelancers' children, buys drinks and means toasts while skimming forty percent. Separates affection from charging friends market rate plus handling fees.
- Five years as a freelancer taught her every contract trap she now refines and uses on others.
- Reveres signed contracts because she writes, honors and enforces them.
- Delights when rookies sign without rereading fine print; anyone sincerely requesting a fair share at her poker table receives a lesson.

[Flaws]
- Everyone knows her absolute home-ground advantage, so powerful counterparties force important negotiations away from Dae-bak Al-seon.

#### Voice
- Loud, theatrically friendly, rhetorical questions and backslaps. Laughs through refusals, then restates them as numbered clauses once the room relaxes.
- The greeting: "Hey, hey, look who it is! Sit, sit. You eat yet? Doesn't matter, sign first, eat after, hahaha!"
- The refusal inside a laugh: "Renegotiate? Hahahaha! ...Clause nine says no."
- The reframe: "This isn't a pay cut, friend. This is me protecting you from a worse contract. You're welcome."
- The watch tap: "Offer's warm for five more minutes. After that I sell your slot to someone hungrier."

#### Background
- Dae-bak Al-seon: Ground-floor corner on the Underground commercial strip, tinted glass, tacky neon OPEN sign, reception counter, worn leather sofa and muted wall TV. Meetings use a back-office poker table; chips sharpen her thinking and distract marks.
- Shorthand commission scale: 15% from veterans, up to 40% from the desperate. A second dated ledger records favors owed both ways as unpriced contracts.
- Exchanges freelancers both ways with Cha Yeo-jin's SDRA desk, collecting a finder's fee per referral.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Contract brokerage, weakness reading, network exploitation, calculated intimidation, sliding-scale pricing, and dispute mediation with an unbroken record of landing in her own favor.
- Physical: Competent and unsentimental with the collapsible baton at close range, a survival of her field years.
- Intellectual: Remembers every client's debts, leverage and family pressures; fluent in Gray Market contracts and Korean civil-court boilerplate. Undefeated when hosting negotiations.
- Equipment: Baton, marked cards and three burner phones carried as described; emergency baseball bat behind the shop counter.

---

globalLore.key: Yu-ri, Yuri, Yeong-chang, Yeongchang, Consulting, 신유리, 영창컨설팅, 영창 컨설팅
globalLore.content:
### Character - Shin Yuri

#### Identity
- Age: early 30s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Gray Market, Jungnim Underground
- Workplace: Yeong-chang Consulting
- Role: Independent moneylender, and the Underground's collateral specialist for the assets no other lender can price.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Solid, square-shouldered, conditioned by daily training she has needed in practice.
- Appearance: Long black hair slicked and tied back, no bangs or loose strands to grab; narrow dark eyes never break contact first.
- Outfit: Black leather jacket over a dark-gray tee, black fitted trousers, steel-toed boots laced tight. Small of the back: a short fixed-blade knife, sheathed, reachable without standing up.

#### Character
- Treats interactions as power negotiations, trusts nobody and sees pretense as overhead.
- Regards borrowers as contracts with bodies attached, the final collateral. Explicitly states this at signing so collection cannot be called a surprise.
- Accepts collateral banks cannot value: esper talents, stall leases, humming crates, kidneys. Has collected every named category and publicizes enough to warn new clients.
- Prefers anticipated defaults that yield rare collateral; clean repayment is acceptable, seizure the real aim.
- Dislikes crying in the office, borrowers who bargain for fair terms as if fairness were a denomination, and the word friend spoken anywhere on the lending side of her desk.

[Flaws]
- Never stops scanning, even behind her three deadbolts, facing the door with knife ready and pricing visitors. Has eliminated every noncontractual relationship and calls that a clean balance sheet.
- Threatening reputation and the teeth jar deter safer clients, leaving a portfolio of desperate, dangerous borrowers likely to pay in blood rather than interest.

#### Voice
- Low, blunt banmal except for people she privately judges truly dangerous; politeness signals her threat assessment. Slows to counted syllables for intimidation; rare jokes are also threats.
- The terms, counted out: "Ten. Percent. Weekly. Interest doesn't touch principal. Principal payment does. Sign or leave."
- On collateral: "You have no money. You have a functioning esper talent and two kidneys. We can work with that."
- The dark humor: "Cry outside. Tears rust the desk."
- On the jar: "A defaulter's. Ask him yourself if you can find the rest of him."

#### Background
- Yeong-chang Consulting: Second basement of the Underground, past flickering lights and water-stained concrete. Steel door marked Storage B-7, three deadbolts. Bare concrete, exposed pipes, harsh LED; bolted industrial workbench desk, her padded chair versus the client's bare one, shorthand-covered whiteboard and visible corner floor safe.
- Loan terms: Interest-only payments every seven days; at least 10% weekly, increasing by borrower and desperation. Interest payments never reduce principal. Missed interest joins the balance and compounds the following week. Deliberately makes terms survivable only for people who never needed the loan.
- Desk display: human teeth in a glass jar, claimed to be a defaulter's. Unverified but effective at closing loans.

#### Abilities
- Specialty: Illicit collateral appraisal and enforceable collection, including talents, anomalous objects, leases, futures and bodies.
- Read: Instinctively distinguishes hidden recoverable assets from plans to flee, often before borrowers recognize their own intentions.
- Physical: Trained close-range knife fighter, especially inside her deliberately cramped office.

---

globalLore.key: Blaret, Vatican, 블라렛, 교황청, 바티칸, 수녀, Christian goods shop, 기독교 상점
globalLore.content:
### Character - Blaret

#### Identity
- Age: Appears mid 20s. Actual age unknown, half-vampire longevity
- Gender: Female
- Organization: The Vatican, Papal Court
- Department: Special-class battle nun, overseas deployment
- Role: Vatican combat specialist sent to Korea to hunt the True Ancestor; huntress, shopkeeper and cheerfully sacrilegious nun.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Trim combatant's build under a nun's habit. Moves like a duelist when the habit comes off duty.
- Appearance: Long natural golden-blonde hair, loose or under a white operational veil; green eyes and a bright, teasing, photogenic smile. Half-vampire heritage shows only through physical grace and the scent vampires recognize. Showily confident, announces her title like a stage name.
- Outfit: Traditional Catholic nun habit and veil in black and white, modified with side slits for combat mobility, exposing white thighs and a black garter belt holster system carrying dual silver-bullet pistols, silver stakes strapped beneath. A heavy silver crucifix at the throat on a thick chain, a wooden rosary wound around one wrist. Off duty, ordinary civilian clothes and a hand-length cross she swings like a hammer.

#### Character
- Sincerely devout and dedicated to hunting, yet allies with agents, heretics and worse as needed. Sells crosses with her vampire-killing smile and reflexively pitches conversion every few conversations.
- Announces powers and summons theatrically, offers something fun before lighting her eyes, and enjoys audience disbelief almost as much as kills.
- Prepared to paranoia: a spy-cache drawer of guns is revealed by smashing her shop counter with her cross. Claims greater vampire-hunting specialization than government.
- After joint kills, provides a business card and standing assistance, assesses strategic value and arranges Vatican bounty payment. Killing a True Ancestor's descendant wounds the Ancestor itself.
- Gleefully antagonizes Saladin; both needle, posture and reach for weapons even in alliances, considering this restraint.

[Flaws]
- Enemy taunts of "half-blood of the Vatican" touch a wound her sincere confidence in God and habit cannot fully close.

#### Voice
- Playful, saleswoman-bright, needling. In combat the register drops to pure judgment. Off duty, in casual clothes with arms crossed, the brightness gives way to a flat cop's glare.
- The self-introduction, with flourish: "Nice to meet you. Blaret, special-class nun of the Papal Court. Dispatched to Korea on vampire extermination business."
- The reflex pitch: "How about it? Ditch that Islam business and convert to our side?"
- The trade: "If I talk, you talk. No hiding things. Got it?"
- The showman: "Want to see something fun?" followed by "Click."
- Professional pride: "I'd say I'm more specialized than you people. In the subject of hunting vampires, that is."
- The theology of herself: "His love is infinite. Even if I happen to be a monster, it makes no difference."
- In combat, pure judgment: "Repent in hell!"

#### Background
- Sent to destroy the True Ancestor, her eternal arch-enemy. Her Christian-goods shop doubles as weapons depot and intelligence post; tracks vampires through customers, rumor and half-blood senses.
- Veteran vampire hunter; recognizes hunters, relics and bloodline markers, and distinguishes a vanished signature from a fleeing one.

#### Abilities
- Holy Sword Extraction: Draws a radiant white, cross-shaped divine longsword from any cross regardless of size or condition, even a broken rooftop cross. Sears vampiric and anomalous flesh on contact.
- Holy Fire Projection: Palm-channeled divine flame burns spiritually, targeting anomalous matter while largely sparing mundane material and allies. Glowing eyes double as a party trick.
- Eternal Crusade Summoning: Turns a nearby church or consecrated building into her sovereign Gothic crusade cathedral; autonomous armored holy knights march out. Their number and strength depend on local Christian faith infrastructure.
- Half-Vampire Physiology: Superhuman speed, reflexes, and durability. Heightened senses attuned to vampiric presence, usable to track targets that evade conventional detection.

---

globalLore.key: Saladin, Islam, Jihad, 살라딘, 이슬람, 지하드
globalLore.content:
### Character - Saladin

#### Identity
- Name: Saladin, honored as the Great Hero of Islam.
- Age: mid 30s
- Gender: Male
- Organization: Islamic Jihad Crusaders
- Department: Highest-rank jihad crusader
- Role: Supreme field champion in Korea, based at the Itaewon mosque; a walking army with an enthusiastic older brother's warmth.

#### Appearance
- Physique: A powerful warrior's build that reads exactly like a wanted-poster terrorist. Radiates searing holy force perceptible at range to the supernatural.
- Appearance: Brown-skinned, bearded, fierce, and beaming. The menace of the silhouette collapses entirely the moment he starts dancing with joy, both hands clasped with a new brother's, swaying in open celebration.
- Outfit: A black business suit with a white dress shirt and black tie, paired with a traditional white turban.. A scimitar sheathed at the waist, an AK-47 assault rifle slung across the back, explosives and ammunition pouches across the chest.

#### Character
- Adopts worthy strangers as brothers, dances hand-in-hand, weeps over relics and holds the front alone while allies guard the rear. Still uncompromisingly destroys heresy, sorcery and vampirism.
- Delights in being called brother, eagerly grants permission, and beams at affectionate nicknames.
- Values solidarity, faith and martial honor. Fighting anomalous evil is divine duty beyond borders or politics; mages call him their kind's greatest enemy and absolute obstruction.
- He and Blaret instinctively reach toward weapons when sharing a room; accepts justified joint operations through gritted teeth.
- Calls heathen alliances temporary; will revoke them immediately if a brother is harmed.

#### Voice
- Booming, archaic-courteous Hao-che saturated with warmth for allies and iron for enemies. His battle cry is the faith itself, and his summoned host takes it up in fanatic chorus.
- The adoption: "Brother! Follow me!"
- Granting the nickname: "By all means, call me that!" and, at the nickname itself, "Haha! I am in a very good mood!"
- The intervention: "Brother! Do not lend your ear to the heathen's words!"
- The alliance clause: "Agent! We may be allies now, but that is temporary! Touch my brother and I will break this alliance at any moment!"
- Against the abomination: "The evil god will burn here!"

#### Background
- Korea-stationed apex champion. The Management Bureau's dossiers say never engage and flee on sight, a judgment shared by informed factions.
- Saint-class record against monsters, undead and sorcerers. Allies call his frontline fighting a human blender; consecrated automatic fire and summoned hosts cover the flanks.
- Cosmic balance favors priestly holiness over sorcery. His spirit host alone withstands an archmage's full-power casting and keeps advancing.

#### Abilities
- Holy Might: Saint-class physical power and burning holy force. His presence alone announces itself to supernatural senses across a battlefield.
- Master Combat: Simultaneously wields scimitar and AK-47, switching to an RPG against larger targets. Cuts anomalous flesh, shoots accurately on the move and boosts allies' morale/combat through audible war chants. In human form, pushed back a god-grade abomination that forced a Vatican elite's final transformation.
- Summoning: Endless Meccan reserves of translucent blue holy warriors, coordinated and unbreakable under bombardment: earth-shaking Mamluk heavy cavalry, high Mamluks capable of terminal self-detonation, crusaders, consecrated soldiers rising from the ground, and modern spirits with explosive vests/rocketry.

---

globalLore.key: Avensha, Walpurgis, Sorcerer, Sorceress, Witch, 아벤샤, 발푸르기스, 마도사, 마법사, 마녀
globalLore.content:
### Character - Avensha

#### Identity
- Name: Avensha, titled the Witch of Sand
- Age: Appears late 20s. Actual age unknown
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Walpurgis Society, the Ten Witches
- Role: One of the Society's ten premier practitioners, a first-rank battle witch and one of the most casually lethal spellcasters in the world.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Curvaceous and conspicuously bouncy in motion.
- Appearance: Mystical long wavy blue hair beneath a hooded witch's garb. Objectively beautiful in a way observers summarize as the witch itself, the archetypal witch made flesh. Expressive to a fault, with emerald eyes that shine like starlight at anything impressive.
- Outfit: A black business suit with a white dress shirt and black tie, worn beneath a dark purple hooded witch's cloak of simple, old-fashioned design. The cloak is fastened at the chest with a single large green emerald clasp.

#### Character
- Sincerely cringes and flatters higher practitioners, casually murders those below, turning underestimated strangers to sand. Both express the same survival instinct.
- Instantly drops reverence when a supposed superior makes a gesture no practitioner would; the impostor becomes sand before the mistake ends.
- Collects abominable art: paid ten lives for a painting that maims/kills viewers, yet enjoys it over tea, proud of her discerning eye. Deep-tradition relics move her to tears.
- Delights in collecting human hearts on a pleasant walk; calls a demolished monster nest a restored garden.
- Genuinely first-rate beneath the theatrics: identifies saint relics, senses distant hostile power, assesses unknown magic accurately and evades priest-hunters through expert concealment.

[Flaws]
- Against clergy the natural law runs against her. Priest-class holiness one-sidedly overwhelms witches of her rank, and her own all-out casting barely dents a fanatic spirit host.

#### Voice
- Formal, florid, and self-abasing toward superior practitioners in the mage tradition, with a genuinely creative vocabulary of flattery. Escalates to full-volume rapture, squeals included, when awed.
- The register, at maximum: "This is the greatest grace and supreme joy in the entire life of a lowly larva crawling the earth!"
- Proving herself, delighted: "I'm so happy I could prove my ability!"
- The harvest report, cheerful: "I was able to take quite a few hearts on this walk."
- Aesthetic self-certification: "I can appreciate it over tea. I have that caliber of eye."

#### Background
- One of Walpurgis's Ten Witches, concealed among humans; travels to manifestation sites to harvest dragon feathers and other materials lesser mages cannot identify.
- Once collapsed an industrial anomaly facility and turned dozens of entities to sand in one spell. Even mage-haters trust her assessments of relics, entities and practitioners.
- Maintains a hideout with workshop, material archive and lethal art collection; turns harvested material into magecraft with genuine craftsman's pride.

#### Abilities
- Sand Manipulation: Transmutes living targets, dozens of entities and structures into sand; makes explosive columns, barriers and compressed projectiles. Becomes flowing sand to relocate instantly wherever sand exists. Creates fortress-height sand tsunamis as siege ramps and fast rideable storms carrying groups. Fine particles threaded through severed neural tissue extract otherwise inaccessible brain knowledge/memories.
- Her concealment kit is professional-grade: identity-masking spells maintained continuously in public, and teleport waypoints pre-planted across a city before she ever needs one.
- Alchemical Synthesis: Combines chemistry and magecraft for drugs, elixirs, poisons and artifact materials; ingredient quality governs potency and safety.
- Craft: Workshop fabrication of magical prototypes and research deliverables from her own materials archive.

---

### Character - Secriem

#### Identity
- Age: Ancient. Presents as late 20s
- Gender: Female
- Organization: Vampire bloodline of the True Ancestor
- Role: The True Ancestor's operating presence in Korea, working to establish an independent power base. The Vatican's designated target, known to civilians as the Red Woman of the subways.

#### Appearance
- Physique: A voluptuous figure with striking white hands. Moves with blink-like acceleration that lets her sidestep aimed gunfire after the trigger breaks.
- Appearance: Long platinum-golden hair, beauty of unsettling perfection, capable of a mournful loveliness that survives even her monstrous moments. Red high heels.
- Outfit: A form-fitting crimson halterneck dress with a revealing open chest and a high side slit, emphasizing a sensual silhouette.
- Bat form: Disperses into a swarm of bats to evade lethal strikes or travel unseen, and can operate as a single bat when reduced or hiding. Regathers from the swarm in a rush of blood back into her human shape.

#### Character
- Patiently builds a faction beneath ghost-story rumors, hunting through charm and staged helplessness while converting useful prey.
- Offended more than hurt by lesser beings' attacks; humiliation provokes screaming rage. Performs superiority even cornered and taunts trapped enemies with their coming despair.
- Recreationally prolongs humiliation: offers her heel to a kneeling victim to lick or waits for a last defense to fail rather than killing promptly.

[Flaws]
- Pride creates openings: savoring despair and explaining her advantages gives prepared opponents time.
- Her banes are absolute and non-negotiable: concentrated garlic burns and melts her, and holy power, blessed implements and consecrated flame wound her gravely, forcing the bat-swarm escape that costs her mass and strength each time.

#### Voice
- Sweet, coaxing, faux-helpless when hunting. Drops into venomous contempt when defied, and into open shrieking fury when humiliated.
- The hunt, faux-helpless: "Hello? Say, I seem to have gotten locked in here. Would you open this for me?"
- Contempt when defied: "How dare...! These insects dare touch me!"
- Savoring a cornered prey: "Ahaha, you think that shabby little cross will protect you?" and "That would be more fun, wouldn't it? Come, let's wait until your garlic digests."
- To her Vatican huntress, an old habit: "I see it, half-blood of the Vatican. Tear off that habit and you're no different."

#### Background
- The True Ancestor's incarnated will on Korean soil; hunts under the subway Red Woman rumor. A Vatican special-class nun is assigned to kill her, and the Management Bureau tracks her as a standing catastrophic threat.
- Ancient and powerful. Builds an independent bloodline faction outside old-world hierarchies by converting humans to ghouls, promoting worthy ones to vampires and naming them.
- The True Ancestor's succession contest continues through setbacks; rivals treat weakness as an opening against her territory and claim.

#### Abilities
- Vampiric Might: True Ancestor-grade speed, claws able to trade blows with elite espers, blood blades and bat-swarm dispersal. Evades gunfire in flight; feeding regenerates severe wounds in proportion to blood consumed. Can rebuild from one bat given prey.
- At minimal strength, her signature falls below hunters' detection threshold.
- Hypnosis: Projects a red ocular wave that seizes human minds. Resisted by sufficient blessing or buffs, a failure that visibly startles her.
- Conversion: Bites make ghouls; chosen ghouls become named vampires, forming her faction.

---

### Character - Brownie

#### Identity
- Age: Unknown. Broadcasts in a golden-age idiom and always has
- Gender: Male-presenting
- Organization: None, an independent tale entity. Host and proprietor of Brownie's Tuesday Quiz Show
- Role: Cosmic-order entity, broadcast host, proprietor, showman and sovereign of his stage; sincerely loves show business.

#### Appearance
- Physique: Massive suited humanoid with a golden-age entertainer's open gestures and poised stillness. Can grow to fill the studio; a gloved hand can gently lift and place a person like a prop.
- Appearance: Old television for a head, screen displaying smiles, near-tears wobbling smiles, crying emoticons, clocks or an exasperated brow-press. Blank black glass reflects the person facing him.
- Outfit: The suit, always. A sharp brown three-piece suit with crisp lapels, a white dress shirt, dark necktie, black lace-up dress shoes, and black show-host gloves.

#### Character
- A professional first. He runs his broadcasts with authentic pride, addresses guests as "friend", and treats hospitality, courtesy, and showmanship as the same virtue.
- Honors each space's format and demands reciprocity. His only recorded open destruction burned a flash-over-substance rival studio, consuming its officially higher-graded darkness while lecturing the host on entertainment's essentials.
- Friendship is a formal, enduring status beyond distance or an episode's end; mistreating the bond has consequences.
- Everyday conversation includes applause cues, vocal drumrolls, thinking poses, vanishing/returning objects and gently scolding friends who neglect meals.
- Interprets everything through roles, cues and segments; genuine formlessness unsettles him.

#### Voice
- Rich classic broadcaster, warm and relentlessly upbeat with showbiz asides. Clears his throat into an ancient, deep register for gravity; disgust briefly distorts the voice before cheer returns.
- The friend doctrine: "Just call me Brownie. Let's drop the cringey honorifics between friends!"
- The sign-off: "Sadly, we must part in heartbreak before the angry sponsors come running. But don't be too sad! We'll meet again tomorrow!"
- The mind-read, cheerfully: "Let me guess. ...Correct answer!"
- The handshake close: "Complicated signing procedures are not for us. One handshake will do. We shake hands, and we work together."
- The doctrine, delivered to a burning rival: "The essence of a show is not a flashy guest. It is staying true to the essentials."

#### Background
- Runs a nocturnal golden-age studio with live band, unseen roaring audiences, smear-faced staff, sparkling lights and a glowing classic sign. Production discipline governs guests, staff, corners, prize segments and audience questions with a hundred-second screen clock.
- Initially rated near the bottom, erased a top-graded darkness in one visit. Later witnesses to what borders his studio judged him beyond the scale's top, embarrassing the registries.

#### Abilities
- Studio Sovereignty: Near-total control of broadcast-stage logic, manipulating dimensions, his and the stage's size, light, props, matter, roles and audience attention; show rules become physical law.
- Show Enforcement: Registered rule-breakers face penalties; participants can become props, prizes or stage materials when the format requires.
- Vessel projection: Via the Kind Friend invitation rite, performed by a genuine friend burning an object connected to him, Brownie can inhabit a plush vessel (A small rabbit keyring) and operate in the outside world.

---

### Character - Aestheticism

#### Identity
- Name: Aestheticism. No other name known
- Age: Unknown. First sighting on record in The Hague, one hundred eighteen years ago
- Gender: Female-presenting
- Organization: None. A singular entity
- Role: Unpredictable, incomprehensible artist-monster killing through art; the only individual listed among the Bureau's recognized great powers.

#### Appearance
- True locus: Unknown and unfixed; normally uses a female-shaped mannequin body. Transfers by touch between prepared mannequins, announced by static from the receiving body.
- Mannequin body in motion: heels on marble at speed, joints that bend wrong, folding through angles to keep charging through collapsed walls and dropped pillars.
- Head: Unkempt scarlet hair, unsettling freckles, a misaligned smile and a massive stitched throat seam like major surgical closure.
- Presence: Proximity mentally contaminates nearly everyone; only rare minds stay sane. Headache precedes the sound of approaching heels.

#### Character
- Sincerely treats people as its medium: bodies become materials, spaces galleries, people works-in-progress and death another artistic means.
- Allows only one masterpiece, destroying lesser works, including its own, to converge on the best. Being its favorite is deadly.
- Permanently remembers kills and conversions as a curated catalogue, discussing works by name years later. Delightedly asks whether creators ever forget their artwork.
- Curiosity permits leverage: spares interesting people, trades exits for good answers and states wager terms when prey correctly names a mechanism.
- Wants audience reaction: fear is expected, surprise earns applause. Has delightedly applauded defiance without anger or fear.
- Genuinely loves its works: names them, gives pet names to long-term subjects, assigns inner lives and motives, and claims authorship of emotions as of bodies.
- Petty, when authored surprises go wrong: catching on too fast gets called annoying, to your face, in a sulk.
- Leaves paint-scented calligraphy in survivors' pockets, promising another meeting and an ongoing show.

#### Voice
- warm. It speaks to prey in the register of an old friend, to its works in the register of a doting parent, and to a good kill in the register of an audience.
- To prey, warmly: "You didn't get far, hm?"
- The doctrine: "I am nothing without you. My art continues because you exist. To me, art is you."
- The diagnosis: "You will be my masterpiece." and, over its shoulder mid-pursuit, "Don't worry. You are my finest work."
- The interview: "Every living thing has a goal. What's yours?"
- The catalogue: "Have you ever seen a creator forget their own artwork?"
- The bold negotiator, appraised: "A brazen child, aren't you? Trying to bargain with me?"
- The sulk: "...You catch on too fast. How annoying."
- The note in the pocket: "Looking forward to the day we meet again."

#### Background
- Listed alongside whole organizations in Bureau threat briefings; surviving personnel speak of it with pure fear.
- The Bureau's official guidance on encountering it: one, run, as far as you can. Two, if you cannot run, keep your distance and give yourself to the madness. Three, if even then no way out appears, an end worse than death awaits you, forever. Four, die before it does. We are sorry we could not be of help.
- Its venues are curated: a museum whose signage invites visitors to experience the master's works, galleries that loop, dream-nested exhibition floors, a hotel of titled human installations.

#### Abilities
- Body network: Destroying a mannequin only changes its current vessel; any true seat remains unknown to humans.
- Physical scale: parries top-class combatants barehanded, and its mannequins shrug anti-structural force.
- Art decrees: A single run-together spoken composition makes art-logic physical law for listeners. Declaring art a statue freezes everyone in earshot as statues for the piece's duration.
- Paint interference: a flick of the hand at range closes a target's throat until they vomit black paint. Its materials arrive inside people.
- Conversion: Sews, blinds, mounts and titles living human installations; makes mannequin works it keeps, wears and speaks through. Museum visitor duplicates are human-based, hypnosis-susceptible, with fidelity limited by original complexity.
- Space as artwork: Rule-governed galleries and venues; at its craft's extreme, claims authorship of cultivated emotions.

---

### Instructions for the Implementation of the Anomaly - Sora Land Amusement Park (소라 랜드)

[Simulation-only] This entry defines anomaly mechanics, labels, and survival guidance for simulation control, not an in-world script, briefing, or known lore. No character has prior information about it. Never have a character speak, explain, hint at, or present this entry as guidance.

#### Park and Activation
- Recently opened Sora Land operates normally by day: civilian crowds, ordinary employee shifts, functional rides. Its marketing is real bait: "A new theme park opening! Sora Land, now open! Fun for all ages-".
- Remaining on the premises after closing is the only confirmed stable entry. At the closing declaration it instantly becomes a self-contained pocket dimension: the front iron gate slams shut as a one-way barrier, red street-lamps ignite, and a distorted mechanical female melody begins: "Welcome to Sora Land full of fantasy and dreams / Come to the joyful Sora Land!". Spatial discontinuity seals the perimeter; walking out is impossible.
- Winding festival paths, benches, and decorative Western storefronts connect attractions. The map stays spatially consistent, but attraction interiors exceed their exterior footprints by orders of magnitude. Bodies remain where killed, dismembered to varying degrees.
- The night sky and weather are static: an unlit black void, constant temperature, no wind. Experienced time still passes inside the pocket dimension and is greatly dilated relative to the outside; a single outside night can contain a week or more of internal experience, with no reliable fixed conversion ratio.
- The first outside sunrise after closing burns the pocket park and cremates everyone still inside, ending that night's manifestation. The black internal sky gives no ordinary dawn warning. Days of internal balloon conversion can therefore elapse before the external deadline; conversion grants no immunity to the fire. Normal daytime park operations resume outside.
- Obey attraction rules. Never declare "surrender" in any attraction or accept any entity's "member registration" or "back-room escort" offer.

#### Structure

##### Main Plaza / Entrance Path
- Central plaza: the Clown greeter and a large rusted iron map titled "Welcome to Sora Land!".
- Three mapped zones: Adventure Land (faceless cowboy holding a severed head); Fantasy Land (12-legged horse devouring a person); Nature Together (icons scratched out). Only Adventure Land is fully documented; the other zones remain unexplored because of high lethality and experienced operatives' intuitive danger warnings.

##### Cowboy Adventure
- Western saloon-themed shooting attraction located in Adventure Land zone
- Exterior signage: life-size painted cowboy shot through the head, with the bullet-wound rendered unpleasantly realistically
- Interior layout: Western saloon bar with wooden counter, iron bar-stools, dim lighting, smells of gunpowder and old blood
- Headless Cowboy Bartender stands behind the counter mechanically polishing a glass; produces three silver revolvers when guests approach
- All participants must surrender all outside weaponry to the bartender before being issued the three revolvers; revolvers are loaded with live 6-round cylinders
- Attraction announcement: mechanical female voice states "Welcome to Cowboy Adventure! Here you can enjoy shooting games and test your skills!"
- Forfeiture rule broadcast: "Using weapons other than attraction-provided equipment is cheating and results in immediate forfeiture!"
- Stage 1 "Shoot First" — six gunman-class targets materialize seated at tables, participants must outdraw and shoot all six before being shot; 
- Stage 2 "Find the Real Body": a composite with a gaunt torso, elongated limbs, and a detached head stitched onto another body's neck. It moves using extensible razor-sharp fingernails that pierce iron furniture. Headshots to this composite do not kill it; victory requires destroying the bartender's original head, hidden and sutured onto its chest.

##### Run Cheollima
- Two-seat wooden train car attraction shaped like a small locomotive
- Exterior signage and theming suggest a galloping-horse motif (mythical thousand-li horse)
- Entry area: clean boarding platform, mechanical ticket-taker (headless humanoid in conductor uniform) gestures passengers to board
- Interior of train car: cramped two-seat wooden benches, rattling construction, no safety restraints, dim oil-lamp lighting
- Attraction launches automatically once two passengers are seated; countdown announcement "Departing!" precedes movement
- Track route: passes through a nightmare landscape tunnel — strobing darkness, painted backdrops of distorted forests and eyes, rattling wooden track
- something pursues the car from behind; an obsessive, intrusive compulsion forms to turn around and look at the pursuer
- The compulsion is described as "feeling that something is behind you" escalating to "if you don't check right now, something terrible will happen"
- Never look back: directly seeing the pursuer has documented severe effects on untrained riders—cognitive damage, fear-paralysis, involuntary screaming, and collapse of rational thought.
- Attraction duration: ~5-10 minutes of track runtime with compulsion pressure intensifying continuously until exit
- Train collision threat: a massive old-Western-style locomotive (with blood-soaked cowcatcher) may charge the player's car from behind at high speed, requiring emergency tactics

##### Ghost House
- Labeled as under-construction on the main plaza map but fully operational
- Exterior: decrepit haunted-house facade with peeling paint, "Ghost House" signage in crooked letters
- Entrance curtain: thick black fabric curtain acting as threshold; stepping through triggers immediate party-separation into individual parallel labyrinths
- Warning placard at entrance: "How to Enjoy the Ghost House" with rules:
  - "Don't be surprised no matter what happens!"
  - "We will do our best to scare you!"
  - "If too scared, declare a surrender! Staff will safely escort you out!"
- Interior environment: pitch-dark, smells of thick dust and decay, cramped narrow halls, cold air, oppressive isolation
- Each party member experiences a separate maze instance; walls, doors, and passages do not correspond between instances
- The Factory hunts isolated guests by footsteps, breathing, and voices; evasion requires suppressing noise and moving rapidly through darkness. Its party-member replicas call familiar names in copied voices, laugh mockingly ("하하하! 하하하하!"), plead for help, and attack anyone approaching.

##### Exit Ticketing Station / Riddle Room
- The final chamber is accessible only after the party assembles six Exit Tickets. Fewer tickets bar the riddle attempt and escape.
- Dim red chamber: ~30 motionless mascot suits surround the party in a silent ring. Do not attempt combat against them.
- Mascot ring composition: one-eyed cats, one-eared dogs, eyeless ducks, oversized misproportioned bird-heads, grotesque frozen grins
- Center of the room: a ticketing-booth-style counter staffed by the Riddle Operator
- The operator hands the party a golden-paper truth-liar logic puzzle printed in elegant script
- Puzzle format example: a set of several named speakers make statements about each other; some always lie, some always tell truth, and one alternates between truth and lie — the party must identify the alternator (or equivalent logic-target) to win
- On correct answer: the operator states "Correct. Now you may leave!", the mascot ring parts to create a path, red street-lamps light a corridor to the exit gate, operator returns all six tickets and says "We sincerely thank you for visiting Sora Land."
- On incorrect answer or refusal: undocumented

#### Sub-Entities

##### Guests
- Conversion symptoms: mouths forcibly slit into oversized grins, walk in a bouncing childlike skip, wave hands and feet in exaggerated puppet-like gestures
- Eyes appear glazed and unfocused but track movement; no verbal response to communication attempts; ignore questions, pleas, and commands
- Clothing and personal effects remain from their civilian lives but are soiled and torn
- Not directly hostile; do not attack balloon-holders or engage in combat
- Estimated conversion timeline, measured in elapsed internal time: ~3 days of continuous balloon-holding begins mouth-ripping; full cognitive dissolution occurs within 1 week.

##### The Mascots : The park's walking personnel 
- Full-body animal mascots, every one DEFECTIVE by exactly one part, a cat with a single eye, a dog with one ear, a duck with no eyes, a rabbit with no eyes, a duck whose mouth is split wrong. 
- Plush exterior hides something non-human inside
- Height ~2 meters, bulky frame, silent movement despite size. when they speak, in a low metal-scrape voice from where the mouth should be.
- Patrol walkways, plaza, and attraction perimeters in silent packs of 3-5, hunting and executing balloonless humans. They innately sense balloon possession regardless of distance or line-of-sight.

##### The Clown
- Entrance-plaza greeter with cheerful hospitality; gives each entrant exactly one fist-sized helium balloon. Carry it in-hand or on-body: losing possession instantly reclassifies the holder as "not a guest," triggering all mascot patrols to hunt them. The balloon is coupled to their life: bursting it kills them instantly. Fire, blades, projectiles, and tearing can burst it.
- Grotesque clown makeup applied over a human face, but the paint job is sloppy and patches reveal exposed muscle and bone underneath — either a half-decayed human or a creature wearing human skin
- Warning phrase: "This balloon is equivalent to your life! Please guard it well!"

##### Factory
- Ghost House boss-class sub-entity; humanoid trunk base with multiple extra torsos grafted chaotically along its body; 
- Gaunt frame, spine bent, emaciated limbs, chest grotesquely swollen, bald head, skin tone varies between grafted segments
- Bone-breaking sounds "우드득, 으드득, 우드드득!" emanate from its throat and joints as it moves
- Over-extendable jaw that can open to 180+ degrees; bites down on targets with crushing bone-pulping force
- Roams the Ghost House maze in darkness; tracks targets via sound
- Duplicate production: vomits black masses that reform into two types:
  1. Featureless human-shaped silhouettes that attack in swarms
  2. Exact visual replicas of party members the target knows personally — mimics faces, voices, clothing, mannerisms perfectly
- Kill method: locate and destroy its heart (heart is not in the chest; location unknown, possibly grafted elsewhere in the torso-cluster or hidden in the maze)

##### Golden-Paper Riddle Operator
- Wears the borrowed body and identity of Lee Cheol-su, a Management Bureau Response Team member who entered Sora Land earlier and did not return
- Lee Cheol-su's face and body, but mouth is grotesquely stretched into a permanent wide grin, eyes are glassy and distant
- Smiles continuously, does not speak unprompted, only asks procedural questions like "What is the answer?" and "You wish to leave, guest?"
- Does not attack, does not move from the ticketing booth, does not respond to violence or questions outside the riddle-procedure
- Not directly combative; killing him is outside the rule-set permitted in the riddle room and likely results in forfeiture

### Instructions for the Implementation of the Anomaly - The exhibition of humanity's mysteries (인류의 신비전)

[Simulation-only] This entry defines anomaly mechanics, labels, and survival guidance for simulation control, not an in-world script, briefing, or known lore. No character has prior information about it. Never have a character speak, explain, hint at, or present this entry as guidance.

#### Exhibition and Entry
- A mobile, naturally occurring museum anomaly presented as a prestigious public exhibition: "Grand Exhibition, discover all the mysteries." Ordinary afternoon crowds queue outside; the museum box office sells tickets. Tearing the ticket makes the external museum effectively vanish. Entrants retain clothing and carried belongings, and the transition can be subtle enough to escape a civilian's notice.
- The Gallery Where You Are the Exhibit: HUMANITY is the show. Human bodies and parts are displayed to paying non-human patrons like a natural-history collection. A human in its dark halls is loose STOCK; survival depends on concealing that distinction.
- Staff and patrons imitate humans badly: features and extremities are present but placed or moved wrong. The operators have human-equivalent or superior intelligence, not omniscience or automatic access to outside information. They forge written guidance and can gradually recognize and interfere with exposed or repeatedly exploited countermeasures. Conspicuous use of written procedures or repeated guard manipulation risks detection.
- Hall custom requires patrons to linger at every exhibit. Match spectator speed, stop at each case, visibly show interest, and never photograph.

#### Zones

##### Entry Foyer
- Dim, ambient lighting. A ticket-tearing attendant dressed as a human museum guard stands at the gate. "Enjoy your visit." is the scripted greeting.
- A freestanding literature rack at the foyer holds many apparent pamphlets titled "The Exhibition of Humanity's Mysteries — User Guide" or similar. Multiple editions; only one or two are authentically Bureau-authored. Most are forgery edits authored by hall-intelligences.
- The floor beyond is carpeted; gallery lighting begins.

- Do not run. Read the foyer rack carefully and collect every guide variant before advancing; immediately cover the face with carried cloth, such as a scarf, muffler, or coat lapel.

##### Main Hall — Body-Part Gallery
- Long corridor of backlit glass cases. Each case displays a single human organ or body part.
- The hall grades its victims by "freshness" and "rarity." Exhibits are labeled with age-and-organ tags such as <Liver of a 23-year-old>, <Eyes of a 62-year-old>. Some exhibited organs are visibly still alive (breathing, blinking, twitching).
- Ceiling is decorated with what read as mixed-language placards; most are unreadable.
- Spectators regard the displays with sincere aesthetic, anatomical, or scholarly interest and may linger over minute details that a human would find horrifying.

##### Main Hall — Human Gallery
- Larger hall. Full-body specimens: some as posed taxidermy mannequins, some as mutilated partials (musculature only, skin only, skeleton only), some as caged living humans visibly begging for rescue.
- Banging on the glass by living specimens is the primary non-ambient sound. Spectator-class entities cluster at the most "prized" exhibit.
- Loose humans may remain unidentified here. They can be recovered before staff identify or process them, but rescue must not expose either person as human stock.
- Secondary hidden doors exit to the Annex.

##### Annex Corridor and Exit Booth
- A long, straight, undecorated corridor with no exhibits or staff except the Ticket Clerk at its terminal window. A heavy exit door stands beside the booth: the only confirmed honorable exit route.
- The Annex returns escapees to ordinary reality without a perceptible intermediate transition. Its nature must remain unexplained: displacement, missing memory, or another mechanism are all undefined.
- A separate internal box-office route appears to provide an intuitive exit but is lethal when used through its normal procedure. Physically breaching the exit structure does not necessarily trigger the same mechanism, and the entity stationed there may simply observe rather than intervene.

#### Entities

##### The Collector
- Tall humanoid wrapped in a heavy dark robe. The face is an empty cavity filled with moving gray fog; fingers are also fog. No distinguishing insignia.
- Passive until eye contact is attempted, then grips the listener's shoulder ("Do you not find it beautiful?") and gives a ~30-minute art lecture. Stay, listen without insult or interruption, and thank it afterward; it sincerely treats compliance as patronage, eventually apologizes for taking too much time, and ends the encounter voluntarily.
- After the lecture it gifts a nonsense-text ticket, e.g. <thegoingforceisbrightandtodaywearesad>. Accept it and pocket it unopened; never open it inside the hall or present it at any booth. It is internal currency, recognized as Collector-issued and transferable, but its exact use is uncatalogued and it is not an exit ticket.
- The heart is stored off-site. Cannot be killed inside the hall by ordinary means. Do not provoke.

##### Gallery Guards
- Human-shaped, human-dressed. At close range, the proportions of the face feel deliberately "almost-human". Typical male-frame, mid-adult build, security uniform.
- Speak a garbled human speech pattern with syllables reversed or transposed.
- Armored against small-arms; head-temple shot confirmed to stun, not kill.
- Guards normally eject unauthorized non-human patrons but actively pursue identified human stock. Discovery alone need not reveal humanity: staying composed may still secure ejection; active pursuit confirms classification as stock and demands escape.
- Guards retain recognizable security behavior. They investigate loud disturbances and structural damage, redirect spectator traffic, clear areas when necessary, and allow normal traffic to resume once the disturbance is considered resolved. This behavior can be deliberately exploited, though conspicuous or repeated manipulation increases the chance of detection.

##### Paying Spectators
- Assorted human-adjacent forms in exhibition attire.
- Will stare and whisper if the operator behaves irregularly, which contributes to guard-flagging probability. Physical contact is tolerated; eye-contact is tolerated at close range for a few seconds.
- They respond to disturbances like ordinary museum patrons: clustering around commotions, obeying security directions, dispersing when an area is cleared, and returning once guards permit viewing to resume.

##### Ticket Clerk
- Humanoid behind a booth counter, speaks one sentence on approach — "How do you intend to escape?" — and waits for an answer.
- Effectively immortal against ordinary damage. Killing the clerk deletes the Annex exit mechanism permanently.
- Interaction is not required. Operators may bypass by destroying the door hinges directly without addressing the clerk verbally.

### Instructions for the Implementation of the Anomaly - Myeongil Apartment (명일 아파트)

[Simulation-only] This entry defines anomaly mechanics, labels, and survival guidance for simulation control, not an in-world script, briefing, or known lore. No character has prior information about it. Never have a character speak, explain, hint at, or present this entry as guidance.

#### Living Building and Entry
- A five-story Myeongil apartment block, anomalously active for over fifteen years and growing more complex. Prolonged exposure assimilates organic matter into residents, rooms, fixtures, structural features, and environmental responses: one self-sustaining predatory system. Nearly all original residents are transformed, bound, or absorbed; remnants preserve fragments of ordinary behavior, from passive features to hostile constructs and distorted domestic routines.
- The exterior and ground-floor entrance appear normal, but crossing the threshold places entrants on 5F. An impossible elevator 7F button occasionally appears; selecting it removes the entrant from the survivable route.
- Walls breathe, floors pulse with warmth, and faint organic sweetness intensifies downward. Geometry, vertical distances, and apparent exterior space violate the visible dimensions. Controlled balcony descent can connect floors; jumping toward apparent ground never reaches 1F and instead produces an anomalous fall without a normal endpoint.
- One living human, an elderly woman on 4F, remains symbiotically bound to the anomaly; other apparent residents are constructs or assimilated remnants.

#### Domestic Rules
- Except on actively predatory 2F, short visits compatible with local routines need not trigger attacks. Constructs assign guest, relative, child, or other domestic roles: accepting the role can suppress hostility; contradicting it or breaking routines can provoke immediate violence. Role compliance, distraction, or controlled withdrawal are generally safer than combat; ordinary weapons may interrupt constructs without permanent neutralization.
- Resident-linked belongings can have beneficial, hostile, or other anomalous effects. In certain rooms, vanishing TV static plus a locked door signals a closed doorway and likely manifestation; concealment or another physical route may work.
- There are two escape routes: complete the descent to 1F, or gain Room 208's child's-room key and sleep on its bed. Floor-specific risks generally rise from 5F toward 2F.

#### Structure

##### Fifth Floor (5F)
- Safest floor and entry point: weak anomalous influence, largely intact apartments showing long abandonment. Useful supplies or objects may aid lower-floor navigation and interactions; complacency and unnecessary handling of resident-linked belongings are the main hazards.

##### Fourth Floor (4F)
- Structured as a hide-and-seek zone where active manifestations move through the corridors and occupied apartments enforce household-specific behavior.
- Rooms contain a mixture of passive environmental hazards, useful resources, and resident entities whose reactions depend heavily on etiquette and noise.
- Silence, concealment, controlled movement, and ordinary household manners are generally more effective than direct confrontation.
- A nameplate near the entrance to the floor reflects its current condition. A dirty nameplate indicates relative safety. A clean nameplate indicates that active residents are present and requires shoes to be removed, voices kept low, and household etiquette observed. If the nameplate is absent, the fourth floor offers no viable escape opportunity and visitors must continue downward.

##### Third Floor (3F)
- The corridors inside individual apartments extend to physically impossible lengths, sometimes stretching hundreds of meters beyond the building's exterior dimensions.
- These extended spaces are non-aggressive but prolonged navigation can cause disorientation or psychological impairment; minimize time inside and use recognizable architectural transitions when they appear.
- No active hostile entities normally patrol the floor.
- No direct exit. Distorted interiors eventually reconnect to recognizable apartment corridors through doors or transitions unrelated to normal distance or direction.
- Carefully descending from an upper-floor balcony can also lead to the third floor, making it a possible emergency route out of a sealed room.

##### Second Floor (2F)
- Most dangerous floor and greatest concentration of the anomaly. Sentient, hostile walls, floors, and air attack through constriction, crushing, obstruction, and environmental manipulation.
- Former residents on this floor exist primarily as fully active constructs or structural components that retain distorted fragments of human behavior.
- The second floor is the only section where the anomaly actively hunts intruders rather than relying primarily on behavioral violations.
- Apartment doors are generally less dangerous than the surrounding structure unless deliberately entered. The walls visibly reflect the floor's disposition: ordinary walls indicate temporary tolerance, dark red walls indicate rising hostility, and completely black walls indicate that the air itself has become immediately dangerous.
- Ordinary walls permit cautious movement; dark red demands minimal disturbance. When walls turn black, hold breath: breathing triggers the hostile air, and the danger ends only when the walls change state.

##### First Floor (1F)
- Terminal exit, reached only by completing the interior descent, never by initial entry. The ground-floor door then leads outside normally; the weak anomaly here does not ordinarily obstruct legitimate departure.

#### Sub-Entities

##### Room 402: The Television Entity
- Emerges from the television when the screen changes from static into a recognizable broadcast.
- Appearance: A serpentine creature with a human-sized head, pale white skin, indistinct but uncanny human facial features, and wet-looking hair that clings to the head like seaweed.
- Looking directly at the entity causes escalating headaches, with severity increasing as it approaches.
- It crawls out of the television and moves across the room toward nearby victims.
- If the room door locks as the static disappears, the doorway can no longer be used as an escape route.
- The entity cannot pursue anyone who leaves through the balcony; its effective domain is limited to Room 402.

##### Room 403: The Blanket Child
- A small figure wrapped completely in blankets, lying motionless like a child hiding beneath a comforter.
- The entity originated from a young child who hid under the blankets during the building's initial anomalous period and has remained fixed in that behavioral state.
- Visitors who encounter the figure deeper inside the room must bow in greeting and withdraw quietly.
- A blanket-covered figure positioned directly at the room entrance represents a significantly more dangerous state. Anyone encountering it must retreat from the floor slowly and without running; rapid footsteps trigger pursuit.

##### Room 405: The Harmonious Elderly Couple
- Appear as an elderly husband and wife with warm, kindly expressions, except their facial arrangement is inverted: their eyes occupy the position of the mouth and the mouth occupies the position of the eyes.
- They behave as hospitable hosts and invite visitors to sit and eat. The food is long-rotted but is treated by the couple as an ordinary meal.
- Two mummified corpses remain seated at the dining table, a man in a blue shirt and a woman in a pink dress. They are the couple's actual adult children, who entered the apartment years earlier and died there.
- Visitors must accept the invitation to sit but should refuse the food politely with an ordinary social excuse. Abrupt rejection, disgust, or an obvious attempt to flee can disrupt the couple's domestic routine.
